E2 · Canonical Library

the single agreed vocabulary and object model: canonical terms, definitions and their adoption state

Purpose

Keep one agreed meaning per term so lanes cannot diverge on vocabulary.

Strategy

Canonicalise only after collision-checks against the existing corpus; never merge referents silently.

Assets

Canonical definitions, the object index and collision-resolution records.

Mesh participation (all nine stages)

1 Signal — What EntersNew terms, contested meanings and vocabulary collisions surfaced by any artefact.
2 InterpretationWhether a term is new, a synonym, a collision, or a candidate canonical object.
3 StructuringCanonical entries with state (candidate/adopted/deprecated) and lineage.
4 ValidationCoherence checks against the corpus and Steward adoption decisions.
5 Action PermittedRecord candidate canonical entries; publish adopted vocabulary to all surfaces.
6 ObservationWhere artefacts drift from canonical vocabulary in practice.
7 LearningWhich definitions hold under use and which keep producing collisions.
8 Asset ConversionAdopted definitions become durable Canonical objects cited by every other Element.
9 Feedback Returns ToDrift observations return to Canonicalise as correction Signals.
